messages:
Erin: Quick heads-up — I'm putting together a 6-month decoupling plan for the enrichment pipeline to reduce surface-area coupling between request-router, enricher, and session-store. Sharing the lightweight cutover checklist + rollback hypotheses for sanity checks before I turn this into a formal RFC.

Raj: SGTM, can you paste the main success criteria? trying to align with SRE/latency SLOs.

Erin: Primary success criteria: 1) no increase >5% p95 latency on hot routes, 2) <1% error budget burn for the first 48h of each canary, 3) feature parity for top-5 tenants. Secondary: cost should not increase >8% at steady state.

Sophie: How are we handling KV-surface changes? migrating from composite key -> namespaced keys will touch a lot of callers.

Erin: Plan is to introduce an adapter layer (read-through shim) for 3 releases. Phase A: adapter reads both shapes and writes new shape. Phase B: backfill job converts old keys, adapter only reads new shape but still responds to old callers. Phase C: remove adapter.

Taylor: For the adapter, we should add explicit feature flags per tenant so we can roll subsets independently. Also add per-route traffic shaping so we can keep p95 under control.

Erin: Agree. Proposed rollout cadence: canary (1 tenant) -> ramp (5 tenants) -> broad (25% traffic) -> full. Each step gated by automated regression tests + canary smoke that checks: latency, error rate, success rate of sample requests, and a correctness diff of outputs for a prompt sample set.

Sophie: What's the rollback hypothesis? If we see degraded correctness or latency, do we revert routing at the LB or do we revert code?

Erin: Rollback hypothesis: fast rollback should be done via routing (feature flag) to avoid DB migration reversal. If we need code rollback, we must ensure adapter still understands both shapes; so releases must be backward-compatible for the first 2 waves.

Raj: Any data migration windows? backfills need quotas and rate limits to avoid IO storms.

Erin: Yes — we'll run backfills in small shard windows with concurrency limits and metrics: ops.backfill.rate, ops.backfill.retries, ops.backfill.errors. Backfill controller will respect a global throttle and per-tenant windows.

Taylor: Add audit logs for key translations so we can trace mismapped keys quickly. Also add an alert for translation-error-rate > 0.1%.

Sophie: For contract changes between enricher and router, let's version the protobufs and use optional fields. No forced breaking changes.

Erin: Good call. We'll publish a migration guide and include a compatibility test harness (unit + integration) that runs both old/new proto paths during the ramp.

Raj: Any perf microbenchmarks for the adapter? curious about added tail latency.

Erin: I ran a local perf spike — adapter adds ~0.6ms median and ~2.3ms p95 to the hot path when using synchronous translation. We're going to make translation async where possible and add a local in-memory cache for translated keys.

Taylor: Make sure the SKUs for Dedicated customers are documented — they may need different rollout windows.

Erin: Yup, will include dedicated-customer runbooks. Also adding a one-pager outlining ownership handoff: platform owns adapter and backfill tooling, product owns contract acceptance tests.

Sophie: Is there a plan to mark this as technical debt to pay down afterwards? I worry the adapter becomes permanent if we don't schedule removal.

Erin: Will add an expiry date in the design doc and a follow-up ticket: "adapter removal + readonly audit" scheduled 3 months after full cutover. We'll also add an automation that flags keys still being translated after N days.

deploy-bot: Draft RFC created: https://rfc.redwood.internal/r/ENRICH-874 (Erin)

Raj: OK, looks solid. If you want, I'll scope the SLO guard rails and add the canary playbook.

Erin: Please do. I'll draft the RFC tonight and attach the checklist + backfill controller code snippet. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
